newsitem.title: USA: Triarc move seen solidifying position - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Triarc move seen solidifying position - analysts.

text.p: Triarc Cos Inc snapped up the maker of Stewart's root beer on Tuesday in its latest move to solidify its position as a major alternative beverage supplier.

Triarc, which roared into the market recently with its $300 million acquisition of Snapple drinks, gained even more leverage against the soda giants with the relatively tiny $31 million purchase of niche root beer maker Cable Car Beverage Corp.
"This helps them solidify their role as the non-traditional beverage leader," Salomon Brothers analyst Jennifer Solomon said. "I think it's a smart strategic move."
Triarc acquired struggling Snapple from Quaker Oats Co last March.
"They've moved very quickly to give it their own imprint, which is great," Solomon said.
Triarc's other beverage brands are Mistic and Royal Crown, a cola brand.
Cable Car, based in Denver, makes Stewart's brand root beer and other flavors. Its 1996 sales were $18.8 million.

Triarc agreed to exchange 0.1722 share for each Cable Car share. Triarc said in a news release that it expects to issue about 1.5 million shares, which based on its Tuesday price would value the deal at about $31.1 million.
Triarc shares were down 1/8 to 20-5/8 in early-afternoon trading. Cable Car was down 21/32 to 3-3/8.
"It sounds like a really good niche acquisition," Solomon said. "This may even be additive to earnings. If it's dilutive, I think it's only dilutive in the very near-term."
Solomon maintained her "buy" recommendation on Triarc, as did Lehman Brothers analyst Michael Branca.
Branca said Triarc can benefit from synergies when it acquires small brands like Stewart's that fit into the alternative beverage category.
"Triarc management has a reputation for very savvy investments," he said. "In our view, Cable Car should be delighted with the opportunity to participate in Triarc's growth."
The Cable Car acquisition, if approved by regulators and Cable Car shareholders, would close in the third quarter, Triarc said.
